bug: mysql_instance.py stop CLI action reported mysqld_stopped=true without ever sending mysqladmin shutdown when invoked from a separate process than the one that called init-start
root_cause: MysqlInstance.stop() gated the entire shutdown action on `self.process is not None and self.process.poll() is None` -- an in-memory Popen handle that only exists within the same Python process/object that called start(). A separate CLI invocation of `stop` constructs a brand-new MysqlInstance with self.process=None, so the condition was always False and the code fell straight to `else: result['mysqld_stopped'] = True`, claiming success with zero verification.
identity_mechanism_used_for_fix: mysqld's own --pid-file (authoritative, written by mysqld itself, always present while it runs) resolves the target PID across process boundaries. Ownership is verified (never assumed) by cross-checking the live process's Name and CommandLine via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` against this instance's own --datadir and --port strings -- never by PID number or port number alone.
fix_summary: stop() now: (1) treats 'not ping-able' as ALREADY_STOPPED (idempotent, no action); (2) resolves PID from the in-memory handle if present, else from mysqld.pid; (3) verifies ownership via CIM command-line match; (4) always attempts a protocol-level `mysqladmin shutdown` (safe regardless of ownership verification -- it can only affect whatever server answers on that exact host:port); (5) polls until the port genuinely stops answering, up to a bounded timeout; (6) only if ownership was verified AND graceful shutdown timed out, re-verifies ownership immediately before a bounded taskkill fallback; (7) returns STOP_FAILED (never a false SUCCESS) if the port still answers, or if the owned process entry is still present, after all of the above.
hard_guard: MysqlInstance.__init__ raises ValueError unconditionally (not `assert`, which -O strips) if port == 3306 (the app database's port) -- a MysqlInstance can never be constructed against it, so no code path in this module can ever start, stop, or kill anything on 127.0.0.1:3306/laravel.
end_to_end_proof: init-start -> mysqld active, port active, pool create-and-migrate succeeded (4 pool DBs incl. mepa_wave5_test_pool_01 with 152 tables) -> SEPARATE CLI invocation of stop -> independently reconfirmed via mysqladmin ping (connection refused), netstat (port not listed), and a raw mysql client connection attempt (ERROR 2003, connection refused) that the instance is genuinely gone. 127.0.0.1:3306/laravel confirmed unchanged (127 tables) before and after.
adr_0014_classification: TEST_INFRASTRUCTURE. The bug itself never altered product behavior and never affected any completed A1 evidence (all A1 evidence was gathered while the instance was genuinely running, before any stop() call), so it does not retroactively invalidate P0.3.5-A1's PHYSICAL SCHEMA READY FOR INDEPENDENT AUDIT verdict. It is closed here because a false-success STOP result is an EVIDENCE reliability risk for future runs (a caller trusting 'mysqld_stopped: true' could leave orphaned instances or falsely assume a clean environment for the next test session).
